_why: The machine-readable register of THIRD-PARTY BINARY ARTIFACTS that ship
with PATANYX but are not Cargo packages: model weights, prebuilt WASM,
vocabularies. scripts/shipping-licenses.py builds the About panel's
attribution from `cargo metadata`, so it sees Rust crates and NOTHING
ELSE. A shipped .onnx or .wasm appears in no inventory, and the
attribution gate regenerates an identical file, diffs clean and prints OK
while those components ship with their licence terms unmet.
That is not hypothetical. The PP-OCR models below shipped attributed only
by a hand-written NOTICE entry, with no gate verifying it stayed true and
no hash pinning the bytes it described.
MIT, BSD, ISC and Apache-2.0 all require the copyright notice to travel
with the binary. A missing entry here is a licence term unmet, not a
formatting slip -- the same standard attribution-gate.sh already applies
scripts/artifact-manifest-gate.py enforces three things: every declared
artifact exists and still hashes to what is recorded; every file under a
watched directory has a row; and every row carries a licence and a

watched_dirs.note: Every file here ships. A new model dropped in without a row below fails the gate.
The translation engine and its glue. Both ship in the installer; the language models do NOT -- they download on demand.

artifacts.notes: Apache-2.0 covers code and weights, per the upstream project. Provenance predates this register; upstream_version is honestly 'unrecorded' rather than guessed.

Decides 0 vs 180 degrees for a detected crop. Same Apache-2.0 clearance over code and weights as det/rec; models/ocr/README.md records the source inference.pdmodel and pdiparams hashes it was converted from.
Character set for rec.onnx; ships with it and is covered by the same licence.

That record states its own licence, revision and Firefox release, and publishes BOTH the zstd hash (327fcfc7...) and this decompressed hash. Taken from Mozilla rather than browsermt because browsermt has been dormant since 2024-05-12.

Its moz.yaml names the SAME revision as the wasm record, so the pair is matched by provenance rather than by proximity. A wasm and a glue from different revisions fail like data corruption.

OPERATOR RULING 2026-08-30: the model weights are attributed AS IF MPL-2.0
applies to them. Mozilla states no licence for the weights specifically and
the models collection carries no licence field -- unlike the WASM collection,
which states MPL-2.0 outright. When the download path is built, the delivery
manifest is where those hashes get verified; this register cannot do it.
